title: Cap. 6 Arg. 6: Prosper—many hear; wills prepared or not; mercy and judgment in the wills
pass_a_gloss: To this Prosper recalls the distinction of believers and unbelievers (Ad excerpta Genuensium, reply to Doubt 4). "Many hear the word of truth, but some believe, others contradict: therefore these will to believe, those are unwilling. Who does not know this? Who denies this? But when the will is prepared by the Lord for some, and is not prepared for others, it must certainly be discussed what comes from mercy, what from judgment." And a little later: "Mercy and judgment have been wrought in the wills themselves."
pass_b_english: Prosper brings the difference between believers and unbelievers back to the same point (Ad excerpta Genuensium, reply to Doubt 4): "Many hear the word of truth, but some believe and others contradict—so these will to believe, and those will not. Who does not know that? Who denies it? Yet when the Lord prepares the will for some and does not prepare it for others, we must ask what comes of mercy and what of judgment." And a little later: "Mercy and judgment have been done in the wills themselves."
source_text: Huc revocat Prosper discrimen credentium & non-credentium, Ad excerpta Genuens. resp. ad Dub. 4. Multi audiunt verbum veritatis, sed alii credunt, alii contradicunt: volunt ergo isti credere, nolunt illi. Quis hoc ignoret? quis hoc neget? Sed cum aliis praeparetur, aliis non praeparetur voluntas a Domino, discutiendum est utique quod veniat de misericordia, quod de judicio. Et paulo post, Misericordia & judicium in ipsis voluntatibus facta sunt.
